author: 👍's up
title: Lacking key features
content: I used to play a lot of mobile shooters years ago and there are a few details that separate the good from the bad. Fortnite’s biggest flaw (even from before it was originally removed from the App Store) is its lack of touchscreen control customization where it matters. There are no settings to move around and resize buttons making the game practically unplayable with the claw grip on a large display and unfit for many play styles on small displays. I know that is kind of a pain to add since this is a port of the PC game, but it’s very important for any mobile shooter. On my iPad Pro 12in, the buttons take up so much space on the screen that there is no place for my index finger to look around and the buttons are so far apart that it is completely unwieldy to use. The game is unplayable in any reasonable fashion on the iPad Pro as a result. Secondly, I would like to see mouse and keyboard support unlocked, at least on iPadOS. I know keyboard support is in the game as I can navigate menus just fine with my Magic Keyboard. I don’t care if you move me to PC lobbies if I have the setting turned on. I have a laptop grade chip in this “Pro” device, so it would be nice to actually able to play this game comfortably with controls that I am most familiar with like a laptop. Make these adjustments and I will have noting but praises for this app. Until then, this app is only useful for checking the shop.

author: full facts
title: Just as buggy as Fallout 3
content:
This game has probably the slowest input speed and stability I have seen for a mobile game yet, even the old Happy Wheels app is more stable than this (yes, it is that bad.), I mean this is almost unplayable. 
The first thing is the input delay, it has a good 1-2 second delay in button presses or game data. The delay and mapping makes the game feel almost unfinished or W.I.P. or even a demo of a new game, there are times where you press a button and it will either not register or take a second or two to register, Ive literally died due to input delay or button mapping bugging out on me. There are times where you will try to move your aim around while holding down and it will register as you moving your finger out of the button’s hitbox like it is using a different fire mode than the one you chose. 
Game data transfer is another thing, it’ll sometimes freeze up and take about 5-8 seconds to register a chunk of game data, which if you are mid fight will be a death sentence. It should never ever need to do this sort of thing, considering that Call of Duty Mobile has never ever needed to do that. 
Bottom line, this game is beyond broken and could stand to have a full rework to it, maybe even have some devs that helped with CoD Mobile come over and help with it. This game is nowhere near ready for mobile gaming, and needs heavy reworking and help. Some things do work with a lot of delay in input and game data of course, but not nearly as bad as the in game combat or match play. Overall, a solid 3 out of 10, Epic Games should be ashamed, because this is just sad.

I also noticed some lag and overheating on my phone during longer sessions, which is frustrating, especially when I’m trying to stay competitive. What worries me most, though, is that this might not last. Apple and Epic are still fighting in court, and depending on how that goes, the game could disappear again. author: ThegamingNite_YT
title: Fortnite Mobile Needs a Fully Customizable HUD for Touch Players
content:
Congratulations on your recent court case victory in Apple vs. Epic Games a landmark moment with meaningful implications for the entire industry. As a longtime supporter and player of mobile titles, I’ve truly appreciated the innovation and entertainment your Epic games have brought over the years even though I was not able to play for long on the mobile version.

With Fortnite Mobile making a return, I was genuinely excited to jump back into the experience. However, I’ve found the limited HUD button layout customization to be a significant barrier to fully enjoying the game on mobile devices. The inability to reposition key controls such as fire, ADS, crouch, jump, sprint, reload, heal, and other essential actions makes it difficult to play effectively without using a controller.

This issue extends beyond personal preference. Many players, especially those with physical disabilities, rely on customizable on-screen controls to enjoy games comfortably and competitively. Providing the option to freely customize the HUD layout would not only make Fortnite more accessible, but also expand and strengthen the mobile player community.

I kindly urge the development team to consider implementing a fully customizable HUD layout option within the settings. This enhancement would be a major step toward inclusivity and would empower players to engage with Fortnite Mobile on their terms.

Thank you for your time and continued commitment to delivering world class gaming experiences.

Sincerely,

author: nicknamenowdotcom
title: Cheaters in ranked
content:
ESP and Wallhacks: When someone locks onto your exact coordinates through terrain and solid objects without ever losing track of you, they are running overlay software that renders player positions through the map. Human eyes and game audio cannot pierce solid geometry; code running over the game client does.
 Input Interference and Packet Manipulation: When your gun refuses to fire during a critical engagement while your connection is stable, it points directly to exploit tools that interfere with client-side registry, forcing desync or command drops on your end while keeping their inputs fully functional.
 The Lobbystack Problem: Seeing the same behavior, recycled patterns, and impossible tracking match after match makes it obvious why the game feels entirely compromised. When third-party software and memory injectors are active in lobbies, competitive integrity completely falls apart.
You aren't imagining things, and your instincts are right. When software lets someone override the core rules of visibility and weapon mechanics, it isn't a fair fight—it's getting cheated.
